headline: Reducing transcript mapping ambiguity and resolving isoforms from RNA-seq reads
label: Isoform Resolved Transcriptome Analysis
summary: Recent RNA-seq tools target isoform ambiguity, splicing, annotation and editing using transcript-specific sequence features and evidence tiers.
synthesis: The common thread is resolving which transcript a read or signal belongs to. The quantification-focused preprint isolates transcript-specific k-mers to cut mapping ambiguity in isoform quantification, while MOCHI applies a reference-independent k-mer framework to curate candidate independent intronic transcripts from strand-specific short reads. Other items operate on adjacent steps. DirectClean handles artifacts in ONT direct-cDNA reads and rescues recoverable ones, and SQANTI-evidence annotates unannotated genomes from long-read RNA-seq alone. LRP2 links long-read isoform discovery and differential isoform usage to mass-spec evidence. splicelogic converts transcript-set differences into discrete splicing events, scSpAS provides a single-cell and spatial isoform regulation resource, and Edi-Set-Flow addresses A-to-I editing rather than isoform identity.
